answer: Fingerprints are counted in relic, which means the distribution is public, and anchor lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a ripple header, so 205 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
